name: Paramedical Nursing Theory Exam - Practice Test 1

questions.question: Which of the following is the normal body temperature in Celsius?
questions.hint: Normal human body temperature is around 37°C (98.6°F).

questions.question: What is the primary function of white blood cells (WBC)?
questions.hint: WBCs are an essential part of the immune system and fight infections.

questions.question: Which vitamin is essential for blood clotting?
questions.hint: Vitamin K is required for the synthesis of proteins involved in blood clotting.

questions.question: Which organ is primarily responsible for filtering wastes from blood?
questions.hint: Kidneys filter wastes and excess fluids from the blood.

questions.question: What is the average human heart rate per minute?
questions.hint: Normal resting heart rate for adults ranges from 60 to 100 beats per minute.

questions.question: Which medical instrument is used to measure arterial blood pressure?
questions.hint: A sphygmomanometer consists of an inflatable cuff and pressure gauge.

questions.question: What is considered a normal adult resting blood pressure?
questions.hint: 120/80 mmHg is the textbook normal standard blood pressure.

questions.question: Which organ is the primary site of nutrient absorption in the digestive tract?
questions.hint: The small intestine absorbs over 90% of nutrients from digested food.

questions.question: Which blood group is known as the universal donor?
questions.hint: O negative blood has no antigens on red cells, making it safe for any recipient.

questions.question: Which hormone is secreted by the pancreas to lower blood sugar levels?
questions.hint: Insulin facilitates glucose uptake by cells, lowering systemic blood sugar.

questions.question: What is the normal respiratory rate for a healthy resting adult?
questions.hint: The normal adult respiratory rate is between 12 and 20 breaths per minute.

questions.question: Deficiency of Vitamin D in children leads to which skeletal condition?
questions.hint: Rickets is a bone-softening condition in growing children caused by lack of Vitamin D.

questions.question: Generally, after surgical procedures, when are skin sutures removed?
questions.hint: Sutures are typically removed between 5 to 10 days depending on body site tension.

questions.question: Which is the largest organ in the human body?
questions.hint: The skin is the largest organ by surface area and weight.

questions.question: What is the compression-to-ventilation ratio for adult CPR by a single rescuer?
questions.hint: Standard guidelines specify 30 chest compressions followed by 2 rescue breaths.
